paragraphs.source_en: Bran was too frightened to shout. The fire had burned down to a few faint embers and his friends were all asleep. He almost slipped his skin and reached out for his wolf, but Summer might be miles away. He couldn’t leave his friends helpless in the dark to face whatever was coming up out of the well.

paragraphs.source_en: Bran wriggled across the floor, dragging his dead legs behind him until he could reach out and touch Meera on the foot. She woke at once. He had never known anyone to wake as quick as Meera Reed, or to be so alert so fast. Bran pressed a finger to his mouth so she’d know not to speak. She heard the sound at once, he could see that on her face; the echoing footfalls, the faint whimpering, the heavy breathing.

units.source_en: Bran wriggled across the floor, dragging his dead legs behind him until he could reach out and touch Meera on the foot.
She woke at once.
He had never known anyone to wake as quick as Meera Reed, or to be so alert so fast.
Bran pressed a finger to his mouth so she’d know not to speak.
She heard the sound at once, he could see that on her face; the echoing footfalls, the faint whimpering, the heavy breathing.

paragraphs.source_en: Meera rose to her feet without a word and reclaimed her weapons. With her three-pronged frog spear in her right hand and the folds of her net dangling from her left, she slipped barefoot toward the well. Jojen dozed on, oblivious, while Hodor muttered and thrashed in restless sleep. She kept to the shadows as she moved, stepped around the shaft of moonlight as quiet as a cat. Bran was watching her all the while, and even he could barely see the faint sheen of her spear.
